label: Oreskes
title: Beyond the ivory tower: the scientific consensus on climate change
detail: None of the 928 abstracts sampled from 1993 to 2003 rejected the consensus. 75% endorsed it explicitly or implicitly and the rest took no position.

label: Doran
title: Examining the scientific consensus on climate change
detail: 97.4% of the actively publishing climate scientists surveyed say human activity is a significant contributing factor. Across all 3146 Earth scientists who responded it was 82%.

label: Anderegg
title: Expert credibility in climate change
detail: 97 to 98% of the most actively publishing climate researchers support the IPCC's attribution of warming to humans. Drawn here at the low end of that range.

label: Cook
title: Quantifying the consensus on anthropogenic global warming in the scientific literature
detail: Of the 11944 abstracts examined a third stated a position on human-caused warming; 97.1% of those endorsed it.

label: Verheggen
title: Scientists' views about attribution of global warming
detail: 90% of the respondents with more than 10 climate publications explicitly agree that greenhouse gases are the dominant driver. Across all who stated a position it was 85%.

label: Stenhouse
title: Meteorologists' views about global warming: a survey of American Meteorological Society professional members
journal: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
detail: 93% of the American Meteorological Society members publishing mostly on climate are convinced humans have contributed to global warming. Across all members surveyed it was 73%.

label: Carlton
title: The climate change consensus extends beyond climate scientists
detail: 96.7% of the surveyed biophysical scientists whose research is mostly on climate agree. Across all 698 respondents it was 91.9%.

label: Cook
title: Consensus on consensus: a synthesis of consensus estimates on human-caused global warming
detail: A synthesis of the seven studies before it. Agreement spans 90 to 100% and converges on 97% among the scientists with the most climate expertise.

label: Myers
title: Consensus revisited: quantifying scientific agreement on climate change and climate expertise among Earth scientists 10 years later
detail: 98.7% of the confirmed climate experts agree. Across all 2548 Earth scientists surveyed in this repeat of Doran & Zimmerman it was 91.1%.

label: Lynas
title: Greater than 99% consensus on human caused climate change in the peer-reviewed scientific literature
detail: Only 4 of the 2718 climate-related papers in a 3000-paper sample from the 88125 published since 2012 were skeptical. The other 99.85% of them were not.
